articles.title: KKR co-owner Juhi Chawla sides with Lalit Modi, backs IPL calendar shake-up - India Today
articles.summary: KKR co-owner Juhi Chawla sides with Lalit Modi, backs IPL calendar shake-up India Today
articles.content: Kolkata Knight Riders co-owner Juhi Chawla has sided with Lalit Modi's suggestion to tweak the IPL schedule and start it in January. Chawla suggested that the IPL should move away from its March-May slot to allow the players to compete in better conditions.Modi, who was the mastermind behind the inception of the league, recently suggested that the BCCI should rethink the IPL schedule and consider a January start. Modi believes the IPL has grown into such a powerful sporting and commercial brand that it no longer needs a dedicated window in the international cricket calendar.He wants the tournament to prioritise sustainable growth, better playing conditions and greater value for broadcasters and Indian cricket.He also pointed to the extreme summer heat during the traditional April-May window, arguing that an earlier start could improve the experience for players and spectators while opening up better broadcasting opportunities.KKR CO-OWNER JUHI CHAWLA RESPONDSChawla responded to Modi's post on X and said that the IPL has earned the right to influence the cricket calendar. The KKR co-owner questioned the logic behind having the tournament being conducted in the summer heat in India.Chawla said that a January start will give the players and fans a better experience and will benefit everyone involved."The IPL no longer needs to find its place in the cricket calendar. It has earned the right to influence it. So why keep playing the biggest cricket tournament on the planet in the harshest heat? And if the calendar is being reconsidered, why not January instead of April-May?""Better conditions. Better cricket. A better experience for everyone overall! The IPL has evolved. Perhaps its calendar should too now!" read the statement from Chawla on X. (Credit: Juhi Chawla X)While a major shift in the calendar hasn't been reported, BCCI are considering moving the IPL's start a bit earlier to tackle the weather conditions."This year, IPL started around March 29 [28], and it was over by May 31," Saikia told PTI. "Only thing which we are discussing is that during the fag end of the tournament after May 15... there is apprehension of having rainfall or pre-monsoon season starting.""On the other hand, there is hot weather which is not very conducive either for the players or for the crowds.""So therefore, there is a discussion going on in BCCI as well as in our IPL governing council regarding whether we can start the tournament a little bit earlier than the fag end of March."It remains to be seen if BCCI will go ahead with this change from next year.- Ends

articles.title: Farmers protest in Kolhapur against Maharashtra government's Gokul board move - The New Indian Express
articles.summary: Farmers protest in Kolhapur against Maharashtra government's Gokul board move The New Indian Express
articles.content: MUMBAI: Thousands of milk-producing farmers took to the streets against the BJP-led Maharashtra government in Kolhapur, protesting and demanding the rescinding of the state government's decision to give voting rights to four directors appointed to the Gokul Milk Federation.Congress leader Satej Patil and farmer leader Raju Shetty organised the massive protest under the banner of the Sangharsh Morcha, where dairy farmers from across Kolhapur district, along with supporters from neighbouring Sangli and Satara, participated in the march at Dasara Chowk in Kolhapur.During the protest, several farmers brought their cattle, underlining their opposition to what they described as government interference in a cooperative institution built around milk producers. Local lawyers also participated, carrying black flags and banners opposing the government's decision.The protest came against the backdrop of the Maharashtra Cabinet's November 4 decision to amend the Maharashtra Cooperative Societies Act, 1960, allowing the government to nominate five members to the managing committees of cooperative institutions with an annual turnover exceeding Rs 500 crore.Of the five nominees, four will have voting rights, while the fifth will be a government officer not below the rank of assistant registrar without voting rights. The nominated members, however, will not be eligible to contest elections for office-bearer posts..Bombay HC refuses to stay Gokul Chairman polls; four govt-nominated directors allowed to cast votes.The government's decision has triggered a major controversy because of the recent Gokul board elections held on October 19. The Congress-led Samvichari Aghadi won 13 of the 25 seats, while the BJP-led Mahayuti panel secured 12. The outcome gave the opposition-backed panel a narrow majority in the influential dairy cooperative, which has an annual turnover of more than Rs 4,000 crore.Opposition leaders allege that the government has introduced the amendment to alter the electoral arithmetic after the Mahayuti failed to secure a majority. With four government-nominated members enjoying voting rights, the ruling alliance could potentially increase its strength from 12 to 16, against the 13 elected Congress-led panel directors.The Opposition alleged that the state government's decision was an attempt to overturn the mandate of nearly 5.5 lakh milk producers represented through the cooperative's electoral process.The controversy intensified after the election of Gokul's chairman was stalled because of a lack of quorum. Under the cooperative's bylaws, at least 14 directors are required to be present for the chairman's election. The 12 Mahayuti-backed directors remained absent from the earlier meeting, preventing the 13-member opposition-backed group from completing the process.Meanwhile, the Bombay High Court refused to stay the state government's decision and allowed the election of Gokul chairman on November 10, 2026. The court asked that the votes of state government-appointed directors be kept in a sealed cover. The entire election process must also be video-recorded. The election result will be declared, but its validity will remain subject to the final outcome of the court proceedings scheduled for November 25..Gokul takeover row: Maharashtra move to appoint five directors sparks political clash

articles.title: Indian sports wrap, November 9: Schedule announced for KIYG 2026; Atiqa Mir shines on FIA Worlds debut - Sportstar
articles.summary: Indian sports wrap, November 9: Schedule announced for KIYG 2026; Atiqa Mir shines on FIA Worlds debut Sportstar
articles.content: Chennai MORE SPORTS Hyderabad to stage 22 of 27 competitive sports as softball debuts and sailing features as a demonstration event Sports Minister Dr Mansukh Mandaviya on Monday announced the full schedule of the Khelo India Youth Games 2026, to be hosted by Telangana from December 11-22. The Games will feature 27 competitive sports and one demonstration sport. Venues in Hyderabad, including the Lal Bahadur Shastri Stadium complex and the Gachibowli sports complex, will stage 22 sports. The rest will be held in Khammam (archery), Hanumankonda (athletics), Karimnagar (judo), Nizamabad (table tennis) and Mahbubnagar (kabaddi). Around 6,000 athletes and 1,800 support staff are expected at the 12-day event, the first Khelo India event hosted by Telangana. Softball debuts as a competitive sport, while sailing makes its first appearance as a demonstration event. “I am very excited to announce the schedule of Khelo India Youth Games 2026,” said Dr Mandaviya. “Since KIYG are coming at the back of the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, we can expect to see some quality performances.” In the previous edition in Bihar, Maharashtra topped the table with 58 gold medals for its fifth title, ahead of Haryana and Rajasthan. -Team Sportstar YOUTH OLYMPICS India’s lone archer at the Youth Olympics, Gatha Khadake, bowed out of the women’s individual recurve U-18 competition after losing a shoot-off to sixth seed Yeeun Whang of the USA in a closely fought quarterfinal in Dakar on Monday. After a gruelling five-set contest ended 5-5, Gatha lost 5-6 (9-9) with both archers scoring nine, but Whang prevailed as her arrow was closer to the centre of the target. - PTI MOTORSPORTS Atiqa Mir produces overtaking masterclass to finish 6th on FIA World Championship debut Indian racing prodigy Atiqa Mir made a stunning recovery on her FIA Karting World Championship debut, climbing 16 places to finish sixth in Race 1. The 11-year-old, the first Indian backed by the Formula 1 Academy, races in the 12-14 category for Kart Republic. Her P6 was the best by an Indian this weekend. Two crashed drivers blocked her hot lap in qualifying, leaving her 83rd of 87. With three heats to recover, she gained 16 places in Race 1, 10 in Race 2 and four in Race 3, finishing 40th overall. In the Super Heat, she started 14th, but a crash dropped her to P16. “That was a lot of fun and I got amazing overtaking practice, that is how I treated this weekend after the qualifying disaster. articles.content: The Smriti Mandhana captaincy era is in full swing in Indian women's cricket as BCCI revealed the squads for the upcoming all format tour of South Africa in December. The tour will see Mandhana take charge as the India Test captain for the first time since taking over the reins from Harmanpreet Kaur.The tour will also see Jemimah Rodrigues return to Indian colours after missing the Asia Cup, Asian Games and the Zimbabwe series with injury. Deepti Sharma will be acting as Mandhana's deputy in the Test and ODI formats, while Shafali Verma will assume the duty in the T20I series.There was also a first call-up to the Test squad for Jintimani Kalita.Mandhana started her captaincy tenure by thrashing Zimbabwe in the T20I and ODI series back home and will be aiming to continue the momentum heading into the women's Champions Trophy in January.India will play one Test, three ODIs and three T20Is during the tour, which will take place from December 9 to December 30.INDIA SQUADS FOR SOUTH AFRICA TOURTest Squad: Smriti Mandhana [C], Shafali Verma, Pratika Rawal, Harmanpreet Kaur, Jemimah Rodrigues, Harleen Deol, Richa Ghosh [WK], Yastika Bhatia [WK], Deepti Sharma [VC], Sree Charani, Sneh Rana, Kranti Gaud, Nandni Sharma, Jintimani Kalita, Sayali SatghareODI Squad: Smriti Mandhana [C], Shafali Verma, Pratika Rawal, Harmanpreet Kaur, Jemimah Rodrigues, Harleen Deol, Richa Ghosh [WK], Yastika Bhatia [WK], Deepti Sharma [VC], Sree Charani, Vaishnavi Sharma, Kranti Gaud, Nandni Sharma, Jintimani Kalita, Sayali SatghareT20I Squad: Smriti Mandhana [C], Shafali Verma [VC], Jemimah Rodrigues, Harmanpreet Kaur, Niki Prasad, Richa Ghosh [WK], G. articles.content: Hyderabad: The Union Minister of Youth Affairs and Sports, Dr Mansukh Mandaviya, on Monday announced the full schedule of the Khelo India Youth Games 2026 in Hyderabad. To be hosted by Telangana from December 11-22, KIYG, a flagship event of the sports ministry, will feature 27 competitive and one demonstration sports. Various venues in Hyderabad, including the Lal Bahadur Shastri Stadium complex in Basheerbagh and the modern Gachibowli sports complex, will stage 22 medal sports while the remainder will be hosted by Khammam (archery), Hanumankonda (athletics), Karimnagar (judo), Nizamabad (table tennis) and Mahbubnagar (kabaddi). “I am very excited to announce the schedule of Khelo India Youth Games 2026. This will kick off a series of Khelo India events that have over the years provided a platform for talented athletes to showcase their prowess and then traverse on the pathway to excellence through our schemes. Since KIYG are coming at the back of the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, we can expect to see some quality performances,” said Dr Mandaviya. Close to 6000 athletes and 1800 support staff are expected to participate in the 12-day sports carnival to be hosted by Telangana for the first time in the history of Khelo India events. Softball will make its debut as a competitive sport while sailing has been included for the first time in the KIYG programme. It will be a demonstration event. “Our PM Narendra Modi has said that the sporting ecosystem must expand in such a way that we participate in greater number of sports at the Olympics. PM Modi also said that we must promote sports played using our natural resources like seas and mountains. Sailing is one such sport and we are extremely happy that our sailors will be part of the Games and help promote their sport,” said Dr Mandaviya. The previous edition of the Khelo India Youth Games were held in Bihar from May 3-15, 2025. Maharashtra defended their Khelo India Youth Games title after topping the medals tally with 58 gold medals, 47 silver and 53 bronze. It was their fifth KIYG title and the third on the trot. Haryana, who have won two KIYG titles, finished second with 39 gold medals, 27 silver and 51 bronze, while Rajasthan were third with 24 gold, 12 silver and 24 bronze medals. As many as 26 records were created in the Bihar edition. Eight were created by girls, out of which five were national youth records in weightlifting. The following 27 sports will be in the competitive category in the Telangana Games: Archery, athletics, badminton, basketball, boxing, cycling, fencing, football, gatka, gymnastics, hockey, judo, kabaddi, kalarippayattu, kho-kho, mallakhamb, rowing, shooting, swimming, softball, table tennis, tennis, thang ta, volleyball, weightlifting, wrestling and yogasana.
